A.reason: A CPPI-style multiplier with a stress-floored reserve, a 5% cash floor and a guaranteed minimum daily swap gives a credible drawdown case, but the 4%/day one-way cap sits exactly at the 20% weekly limit, the rolling 504-day peak lets drawdown build up in steps (the idea concedes this), and growth is modest.

B.reason: A 3.5%/day slew limit leaves clear headroom under 20% per week, a minimum trade pushes toward target every day, and a steep drawdown droop on a roughly 4.5%-vol book plus an all-time 15% backstop make the drawdown case convincing, but expected growth is only about 3-4%.

C.reason: It stays fully invested and rotates into bonds on turbulence, which is weak protection when stocks and bonds fall together as in 2022; the 12% backstop fires late; and the three-trading-days rule depends on 'rarely' having a small gap rather than a guaranteed rule.

D.reason: It combines an explicit risk budget across growth, duration and real assets, a stress-day covariance, a trend gate to cash, a 5% vol target and a graded brake starting at 3% drawdown, with a turnover cap that counts drift; this gives the best balance of diversification, drawdown control and growth, though it lacks an explicit minimum-trade guarantee.

E.reason: A simple, testable inverse-vol trend portfolio with clear turnover and trading-day rules and more growth potential at 8% vol, but the governor only starts at 10% drawdown and reaches its 0.3 floor at 18%, which gives a thin margin under 20% when the 4%/day ramp is slow.

F.reason: Top-5 dual momentum with slow-moving sleeves concentrates holdings and is exposed to momentum crashes, and a governor that only halves risk at 12% drawdown makes both diversification and the sub-20% drawdown the least credible of the six.
